questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanting to learn the language, already knowing friends in the city, curious about the cultural life in the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. And if I didn't find the information I needed, I emailed the host university and they anwered relatively quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a tutor from the host university that I could ask questions about the city and the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There is an international office where you can ask questions. Only problem was that sometimes they would cancel your appointments without warning, but I always managed to get the answers I needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If was easy for me because I could use my network in the city. My impression from others is that it can be difficult if you don't know anyone there already.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is recommendable as the campus is outside the city and living at campus is also not very cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with what I found, but many other international students were paying a lot in rent.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing and felt insecure that I was not able to complete the course selection before I arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out an online registration during spring. In July, I selected my courses, but the final selection was not in place until a few weeks after arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email with the international staff at host uni

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not 100% succesful. The problem was primarily that KU (home uni) didn't recognise the courses available to me in host university. Therefore I has to keep sending applications for preapprovals and it felt quite chaotic and insecute. On top of that, my host uni has a rule, that you can take maksimum 2 courses in English in the political science faculty. Therefore, I had to register for courses in other faculties which I could only do a few weeks after beginning the semester. All in all, in the end I got Europæisk Politik recognized, but not Dansk og Komparativ Politik.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware about the language limitations in the political science faculty. They only let you take 12 ECTS in English - the rest must be in Spanish and Catalan or at another faculty. This is quite a limitation if you don't speak Spanish.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a relatively broad variety of courses and political science and sociology were at the same faculty which enabled me to do more sociology than I have been doing at home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I generally found that it was a lower academic level than at KU. Some courses were almost as being back in high school. I also found that local students were less engaged than students at my home university. However, it was very interesting to experience another learning culture and learn about Spanish politics and cases. I do not regret going at all, but academically I was not impressed.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my host uni there were way more groups works and small assignments during the semester, but on the other hand not as many readings. All classes where in smaller groups (max 50 students).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economy of Natural Resources and Climate Change, Social Change and Globalization, European Foreign Policy, Religions and Global Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: From the ones I did, I would redomment Religions and Global Policy, as it was a very interesting and well structured course.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a sports area at campus which is super cool. There is gym, pool, courts of different kinds, a small bouldering area and a lot of different classes like yoga, strength, etc. It is pretty cheap as a student.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Become a member in the gym at campus and go with your friends. Explore endless bars, restaurants, clubs. Take language courses in Spanish or Catalan (Catalan is free at uni).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of nice daytrip opportunities outside the city. Montserrat, Sitges, Garraf, or even the area around campus. For longer trips the Costa Brava is extremely beautiful and of course the Pyreneers.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Spanish/Catalan culture is not so different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn the language! Join the Castellers group. Look for housing with local students instead of other internationals (even though this can be complicated)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes different understanding of time can cause logistical problems, but it was never anything major

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that everything happens in the street and is open for everyone to join

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the language limitations in selection of courses (I think this might only be relevant to Political Science)
Look for housing in the city and not at campus
Don't have high expectations for academic level at UAB

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Practicing my Spanish and learning a bit of Catalan. Enjoying half a year in a vibrant city with endless places to go out and cultural events as concerts, performances etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my courses preapprovel at KU

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
